concept.anti_generic_signature: A 64 mm espresso cup with a 22 mm handle, a 56 mm anti-roll foot, and four captured 10.00 mm steel ballast balls. It reads as a demitasse beside a mug, not a puck, spinner, or gimmick cube.
assumptions: PETG density 1.23 g/cm3. Four 10.00 mm steel balls contribute 16.4 g each; printed mass is measured after the first solid.
N52 8.0 by 3.0 mm contact pull is 17.3 N to steel; 1.2 mm floors produce the return. magnet_floor_mm is the tuner if the first print misses 4.5 to 5.5 N peak.
Steel-on-PETG friction coefficient 0.20 dry converts 1.8 N ball bias and 28 deg faces into 1.9 N detent force.

step.parts has no magnets and no steel balls; CAD authors 8.0 by 3.0, 6.0 by 2.0, 4.00 and 10.00 envelopes. ISO 4762 M3x10 and ISO 4032 M3 exist in the catalog and are unused because the foot is captured by printed lugs.
This run has no VAULT.json; the four mechanism slugs are novel_mechanisms.

build_plan.exit_criteria: All three printable parts generate, sit on the bed, pass 0.4 mm thickness and overhang, the piston travels 4.5 mm in the chimney without a hard clash, upward piston extraction is blocked by the lip, and downward plug extraction is blocked by the lugs.

components.duty: Signature shell, blind landmark, chimney, detent cages, ballast wells, capture lugs. Stays on the desk during the loop.
components.form: 64.0 mm rim OD demitasse with 2.4 mm wall, 1.4 mm rim bullnose, 22.0 mm handle of 8.0 mm section with a triangular inner opening, 56.0 mm foot, 16.80 mm chimney, two detent cages, four 10.20 mm ballast wells on a 38.0 mm pitch circle, and three 2.2 mm capture lugs.
components.interfaces: Chimney bore 16.80 mm. Retention lip 12.00 mm ID at Z=40.0 mm. Mouth 47.2 mm ID. Disc well 10.0 mm deep. Ballast wells 10.20 mm ID, 10.20 mm deep. Detent cage bore 4.40 mm, inner window 3.70 mm. Magnet floor 1.2 mm over the floor magnet. Wall 2.4 mm. Lugs 12.0 mm wide, 3.0 mm radial, 2.2 mm high.
components.name: Demitasse body
components.placement: Origin at foot centre on the desk plane; +Z up; +X through the handle. Rim at Z=50.0 mm. Open foot at Z=5.5 mm.

components.duty: Thumb input and reprint-first wear part. Carries the ramp and the piston magnet.
components.form: 44.0 mm disc, 5.0 mm thick, 0.8 mm top chamfer; 16.40 mm stem with a revolved ramp; 13.20 mm retention flange on a 11.60 mm neck; 8.40 by 3.15 mm magnet well closed to a 6.8 mm aperture.
components.interfaces: Stem OD 16.40 mm in 16.80 mm bore. Travel 4.5 mm. Ramp crest at 2.8 mm travel, 28 deg press face, 14 deg return face, 0.80 mm home dimple, 0.45 mm click drop. Flange 13.20 mm OD below the 12.00 mm lip. Disc-to-mouth gap 1.6 mm per side.
components.name: Crema piston
components.placement: On the chimney axis. Disc top at Z=54.0 mm at home (4.0 mm above the rim) and Z=49.5 mm at full travel.

components.duty: Closes ballast wells and the floor-magnet pocket. Desk contact face. Twists 60 deg onto the cup lugs.
components.form: 56.0 mm diameter, 5.5 mm thick disc with three 45 degree capture ramps and a centre boss that closes the floor-magnet pocket.
components.interfaces: Centre boss 8.40 mm ID facing the floor magnet with 0.20 mm axial clearance. Closes four 10.20 mm wells. Three 45 degree ramps 10.0 mm wide sit on 2.2 mm lugs after a 60 deg twist.
components.name: Foot plug
components.placement: Z=0.0 to Z=5.5 mm for the disc, ramps above, concentric with the foot. Outer face on the desk.

concept.interaction: The cup stays on the desk. Eyes stay on the screen. The index finger finds the handle; the thumb finds the rim and drops onto the crema disc. Press 4.5 mm. Breakaway is 2.2 N. Peak is 5.0 N at 2.8 mm as two 4.00 mm steel balls crest 28 degree ramps and drop 0.45 mm. That drop is the click. Release lets two 8.0 by 3.0 mm N52 discs, like poles facing, push the piston home. crema_piston is the thumb face. cup_body is the landmark. foot_plug stays on the desk.

novel_mechanisms.definition: A 16.40 mm piston stem slides 4.5 mm in a 16.80 mm chimney. A 13.20 mm flange is below a 12.00 mm lip after assembly from the foot. The 44.0 mm disc is the thumb face and sits 4.0 mm above the rim at home.

Two 4.00 mm steel balls sit in cup cages, each biased inward by a 6.0 by 2.0 mm N52 disc through 1.2 mm PETG. Each ball rides a revolved ramp on the stem: 0.80 mm home dimple, 28 degree press face, crest at 2.8 mm travel, 0.45 mm drop into a 0.40 mm valley. Inner cage window is 3.70 mm so the ball cannot enter the bore.

Two axially magnetized N52 discs 8.0 by 3.0 mm sit on the chimney axis with like poles facing. Plastic floors are 1.2 mm. Pole gap is 7.0 mm at home and 2.5 mm at 4.5 mm travel. Repulsion returns the piston over the 14 degree faces and seats the home dimples.
Three 12.0 by 3.0 by 2.2 mm inward lugs. Three 45 degree ramps on foot_plug rotate 60 degrees onto the lug tops. Pickup cannot drop the plug. No fastener carries capture.

concept.print_stance: cup_body prints foot-down. crema_piston prints disc-down. foot_plug prints outer-foot-down. PETG. Cup and plug cocoa brown; piston beige.
risks: Reversed magnet polarity attracts and traps the piston at the bottom. Mitigation: a raised pip on the closed end of each 8 mm well; like-poles-facing in the spec.
Magnet force through printed walls is a target, not a coupon. Mitigation: magnet_floor_mm 0.8 to 1.6; reprint piston or plug, not the cup.
The piston flange is assembled from the foot before the plug locks; a seated upward sweep is the capture proof.
A catalog bearing would turn this into a spinner. Mitigation: 608ZZ is excluded.
concept.signature_interaction: Thumb press on a crema disc in a demitasse mouth; a 0.45 mm ball-ramp drop at 2.8 mm of travel; magnetic repulsion returns the disc 4.0 mm above the rim.
concept.summary: A weighted demitasse for a desk. The thumb presses a crema disc 4.5 mm; two steel balls crest a ramp at 2.8 mm; magnetic repulsion returns the disc 4.0 mm above the rim.
concept.title: Crema Click

catalog.result: Magnets and steel balls are catalog misses; CAD authors 8.0 by 3.0, 6.0 by 2.0, 4.00 and 10.00 envelopes. Hits iso4762_socket_head_cap_screw_m3x10 sha256 9131c5210d88993bbc37b8050cedda590c55f961e6118af749b70b44a0307f2f and iso4032_hex_nut_m3 sha256 7de90cc2ca5eb2c38a27e3aee66939f30bdfde4ac47cd6f19f0324fcf93496bd are unused: printed lugs capture the foot, so no fastener seat is cut.

research.evidence: Force, mass, wear, and rest numbers follow Halden Detent method. Catalog searches ran against api.step.parts.
research.hardest_to_fake_magic: A weighted demitasse the hand finds without looking, whose crema disc takes a 4.5 mm press, breaks over a ramped steel-ball detent at 2.8 mm, and returns home by magnetic repulsion.
research.limits: CAD and rigid-body sweeps cannot prove magnet newtons, lug friction, quietness, or a successful print. Digital evidence is geometry and clearance only.
research.method: Halden Detent inventor method: one press loop, force curve, mass budget, damped click, named wear pair, desk rest. Selected inventor already bound by Workshop.
rejected_routes: Indexed rotary mill dial (handle becomes the input, not the landmark).
608ZZ spinner in a cup costume (Wish is a clicker; Taste rejects a new outline on a spinner).
Living-hinge crema (a living hinge would carry the primary cycle).
M3 foot screws (catalog hits exist; a printed lug twist keeps capture in geometry and avoids a fastener mount).
